Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n\n## Course conventions (IPHS 400 MP2 rubric)\n\nThese labels are graded and sit alongside the triage labels above.\n\n- **Spec**: exactly one issue labelled `spec` (plus `ready-for-agent`). It must be created before any ticket.\n- **Tickets**: core tickets are labelled `ticket`, extra-credit tickets `stretch` (plus `ready-for-agent`). This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\ntotal 24\ndrwxr-xr-x@  8 maximo  staff  256 Oct  9 18:22 .\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 21 maximo  staff  672 Oct 10 14:39 ..\n# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n\nClick **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\nDo not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n\n## Start here\n\n1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\ntotal 24\ndrwxr-xr-x@  8 maximo  staff  256 Oct  9 18:22 .\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 21 maximo  staff  672 Oct 10 14:39 ..\n# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n\nClick **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\nDo not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n\n## Start here\n\n1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env\nuv run cms serve        # then open http://localhost:8000/admin  -> \"T00: hello admin\"\n```\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\nscripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\ntests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\napp/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\ndocs/adr/          two example decision records\n```\n\nTwo functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\nBoth are graded. self.results.append({\"check\": name, \"ok\": bool(ok), \"detail\": detail, \"fix\": fix})\n\n    # --- checks -----------------------------------------------------------\n    def hygiene(self) -> None:\n        tracked = sh(\"git\", \"ls-files\").splitlines()\n        bad = [f for f in tracked if f.endswith((\".db\", \".env\")) or f.startswith(\".claude/state/\")]\n        self.add(not bad, \"no database or .env committed\", \", \".join(bad) or \"clean\",\n                 \"git rm --cached <file>, confirm .gitignore covers it, then rewrite history if it is old\")\n        history = sh(\"git\", \"log\", \"--all\", \"-p\", \"--\", \".\")\n        hits = sorted(set(SECRET.findall(history)))\n        self.add(not hits, \"no secrets in history\", f\"{len(hits)} match(es)\",\n                 \"rotate the key first, then ask Claude to rewrite history\")\n        self.add((ROOT / \".env.example\").exists(), \".env.example present\", \"\", \"restore it from the template\")\n\n    def docs(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        pairs = [\n            (\"notes/cms-field-notes.md\", \"field notes\"),\n            (\"CONTEXT.md\", \"glossary\"),\n            (\"notes/token-budget-plan.md\", \"token budget plan\"),\n            (\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\", \"usage ledger\"),\n            (\"docs/process/compaction-log.md\", \"compaction log\"),\n        ]\n        if stage >= 2:\n            pairs += [(\"README.md\", \"README\"), (\"scripts/seed_demo.py\", \"seed script\")]\n        for path, label in pairs:\n            self.add((ROOT / path).exists(), f\"{label} present\", path, f\"create {path}\")\n        if stage >= 2:\n            handoffs = list((ROOT / \"docs\" / \"handoff\").glob(\"*.md\"))\n            self.add(bool(handoffs), \"at least one handoff saved\", f\"{len(handoffs)} file(s)\",\n                     \"copy a /handoff document into docs/handoff/\")\n\n    def naming(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        reports = list((ROOT / \"docs\").glob(\"iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_*.md\"))\n        if stage >= 2:\n            ok = any(REPORT.match(p.name) for p in reports)\n            self.add(ok, \"report named correctly\",\n                     \", \".join(p.name for p in reports) or \"missing\",\n                     \"iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md, lowercase\")\n        transcripts = list((ROOT / \"docs\" / \"transcripts\").glob(\"*.md\"))\n        bad = [p.name for p in transcripts if not TRANSCRIPT.match(p.name)]\n        self.add(transcripts and not bad, \"transcripts present and named correctly\",\n                 f\"{len(transcripts)} file(s); bad: {bad or 'none'}\",\n                 \"iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md\")\n\n    def readme(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        if stage < 2:\n            return\n        text = (ROOT /    (\"Generative AI Use Statement\", \"AI Use Statement\")]:\n            self.add(needle.lower() in text.lower(), f\"README has {label}\", \"\",\n                     f\"add the {label} to README.md\")\n        placeholder = \"*(Required. Replace this section\" in text\n        self.add(not placeholder, \"AI Use Statement was rewritten\", \"\",\n                 \"replace the template placeholder with your own statement\")\n\n    def screenshots(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        if stage < 2:\n            return\n        files = {p.name.lower() for p in (ROOT / \"docs\" / \"screenshots\").glob(\"*\")}\n        missing = [f\"{s}-{w}\" for s in SCREENS for w in (1280, 390)\n                   if not any(s in n and str(w) in n for n in files)]\n        self.add(not missing, \"12 screenshots present\", \", \".join(missing) or \"all present\",\n                 \"docs/screenshots/{screen}-{1280|390}.png for each of: \" + \", \".join(SCREENS))\n\n    def git_state(self, stage: int) -> None:\n        tags = sh(\"git\", \"tag\").split()\n        want = [\"mp2-mvp\"] + ([\"mp2-final\"] if stage >= 2 else [])\n        for tag in want:\n            self.add(tag in tags, f\"tag {tag} exists\", \", \".join(tags) or \"none\",\n                     f\"git tag {tag} && git push --tags\")\n        paths = sh(\"git\", \"grep\", \"-l\", '-e', 'href=\"/', \"-e\", 'src=\"/', \"--\", \"*.html\")\n        self.add(not paths.strip(), \"no root-absolute paths in HTML\", paths.strip() or \"clean\",\n                 'use relative paths (\"style.css\"), not \"/style.css\"')\n\n    def tests(self) -> c.naming(args.stage)\n        c.readme(args.stage)\n        c.screenshots(args.stage)\n        c.git_state(args.stage)\n        c.tests()\n\n    failures = [r for r in c.results if not r[\"ok\"]]\n Long tickets get `/compact` at a green test.\n4. **The reviewer must not be the author.** `/code-review` runs in a fresh subagent because an agent that just wrote code approves its own work.\n\n### 0.4 What is given, what you build\n\n| The template gives you | You build |\n|---|---|\n| Stack and dependencies: FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2 hashing, Markdown sanitizer | All 7 capabilities |\n| **T00, already done:** a \"hello admin\" page, one passing test, `cms publish` shipping a placeholder to Pages | Your data model, login, roles |\n| Folder layout and test helpers such as `client_as(\"editor\")` | Every route, form, and screen |\n| Two example ADRs, a security checklist, `CLAUDE.md`, hooks, pinned skills, `check_submission.py`, README skeleton | Your own ADRs, spec, tickets, tests |\n\nThe template contains **no CMS features**. That is deliberate: features are what you are being taught to produce.\n\n---\n\n## Part 1 — Setup\n\n**Time: 45 min. Usage cost: under 5% of a window — mostly shell commands.**\n-----\n\n- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n- What is broken about how they do it now?\n- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n\n### 3.3 The required capabilities\n\nYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n\n1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n\n**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n\n---\n\n## Part 4 — Exercise A: the context-threshold hook\n\n**Time: 30 min.** Full instructions: `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` in your repo. Summary:\n\nYou will finish a `Stop` hook that warns you when your context window crosses 50%, 60%, and 80%, and a `PreCompact` hook that logs every compaction. The status line shows a live meter.\n\nThe rule the meter serves: **`/clear` between short tickets; `/compact` at a green test for long ones**, always with a focus note like\n\n```text\n/compact keep: ticket #5 acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\n```\n\nYour job is `decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py`; seven tests fail until it works:\n\n```text\n/clear\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests.\n```\n\nGraded as B6.\n\n---\n\n## Part 5 — Exercise B: the token budget\n\n**Time: 45 min.** Graded as B7 (3 pts) and discussed in your report.\n\n### 5.1 Why you cannot budget in tokens\n\nAnthropic does not publish a token count for Pro. Usage is metered as a **rolling 5-hour session** plus a **weekly cap across all models**, and what you spend depends on message length, conversation length, attachments, tool use, model, and effort level. So you cannot plan in tokens. You can plan in **percent of your own meters**, and that is what this exercise builds.\n\n### 5.2 The meter\n\nPart 4's status line already reports rate limits when your plan provides them:\n\n```text\n[Sonnet·medium] ctx 52% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░ │ 5h 31% │ wk 18%\n```\n-----\n\n---\n\n#### C. Core CMS functionality — 15 pts\n\n**Definition:** the 7 capabilities work when the judge runs your app from a clean clone and walks through it in a browser.\n**Does not cover:** whether they are secure (D) or pleasant to use (F).\n**How checked:** `uv sync`, `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`, `uv run cms serve`, then a scripted Playwright walkthrough as admin and as editor. Your screenshots are used only if the app will not start, and then at most half credit per item.\n\n| # | Capability | Full credit when… | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| C1 | Login | Seeded admin and editor can log in and out; wrong password is refused with a message | 2 |\n| C2 | Roles | Editor can do every editor task in your spec; admin can do everything | 2 |\n| C3 | Posts | Create → edit → publish → unpublish → delete all succeed and persist across a server restart | 2 |\n| C4 | Pages | Same as C3, and a published page appears in public navigation | 2 |\n| C5 | Admin console | Dashboard shows counts; list filters by status or type; editor shows a Markdown preview (1 each) | 3 |\n| C6 | User management | Admin creates a user, changes a role, deactivates a user; deactivated user cannot log in | 2 |\n| C7 | Publish | `uv run cms publish` regenerates `site/` with only published content, and the Pages URL reflects it | 2 |\n\nEach item: full points if every step passes, half (rounded down) if at least half the steps pass, 0 otherwise.\n\n---\n\n#### D. Security & access control — 8 pts\n\n**Definition:** the CMS resists the basic attacks a public-facing CMS meets, and proves it with tests.\n**Does not cover:** feature completeness (C) or test quality in general (E).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D1 | Password hashing | Stored passwords are argon2 or bcrypt hashes (judge reads the seeded database) | 1 |\n| D2 | CSRF | Every state-changing form rejects a POST without a valid token (judge replays one POST per form without it; 2 = all rejected, 1 = ≥75%) | 2 |\n| D3 | Access-control tests | Tests exist that assert an editor gets 403 (or redirect) on every admin-only route and an anonymous visitor is redirected to login, and they pass (2 = all admin routes covered, 1 = some) | 2 |\n| D4 | Sanitized Markdown | Judge saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the admin preview and the export (2 = neither executes, 1 = one does) | 2 |\n| D5 | No secrets committed | No `.env`, `*.db`, keys, or tokens anywhere in history; `.env.example` present | 1 |\n\nA committed secret also triggers an immediate instructor notification, whatever the score.\n\n---\n\n#### E. Test & code quality — 8 pts\n\n**Definition:** the code the workflow produced is tested, organized, and runnable.\n**Does not cover:** whether the tests came from `/tdd` in the right order (B) or cover security specifically (D).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| E1 | Suite passes on clean clone | `uv run pytest` in the judge's container (3 = 100% pass, 2 = ≥95%, 1 = ≥80%) | 3 |\n| E2 | Tests trace to acceptance criteria | Judge samples 3 tickets; each acceptance criterion has ≥1 test that names or clearly exercises it (2 = all, 1 = ≥half) | 2 |\n| E3 | Organization | Code split by concern (models, routes, templates, services); no source file over 500 lines; no commented-out dead code blocks (2 = all three, 1 = two) | 2 |\n| E4 | Reproducible demo | `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean from `.env.example` values with no manual steps | 1 |\n\n---\n\n#### F. Public site & admin UX — 7 pts\n\n**Definition:** the public site and admin console load, link correctly, and are usable on a phone.\n**Does not cover:** feature correctness (C), or authenticity of design choices (A).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| F1 | Live over HTTPS | Pages URL loads over HTTPS | 1 |\n| F2 | Links and paths | Zero broken internal links and zero root-absolute paths on the published site (2 = zero, 1 = ≤3) | 2 |\n| F3 | Phone width | No horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page and 3 admin screens (2 = all, 1 = ≥half) | 2 |\n| F4 | Admin usability | Clear labels, a success or error message after each save, persistent admin navigation (2 = all three, 1 = two) | 2 |\n\n---\n\n#### G. Your screenshots are used only if the app will not start, and then at most half credit per item.\n\n| # | Capability | Full credit when… | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| C1 | Login | Seeded admin and editor can log in and out; wrong password is refused with a message | 2 |\n| C2 | Roles | Editor can do every editor task in your spec; admin can do everything | 2 |\n| C3 | Posts | Create → edit → publish → unpublish → delete all succeed and persist across a server restart | 2 |\n| C4 | Pages | Same as C3, and a published page appears in public navigation | 2 |\n| C5 | Admin console | Dashboard shows counts; list filters by status or type; editor shows a Markdown preview (1 each) | 3 |\n| C6 | User management | Admin creates a user, changes a role, deactivates a user; deactivated user cannot log in | 2 |\n| C7 | Publish | `uv run cms publish` regenerates `site/` with only published content, and the Pages URL reflects it | 2 |\n\nEach item: full points if every step passes, half (rounded down) if at least half the steps pass, 0 otherwise.\n\n---\n\n#### D. Security & access control — 8 pts\n\n**Definition:** the CMS resists the basic attacks a public-facing CMS meets, and proves it with tests.\n**Does not cover:** feature completeness (C) or test quality in general (E).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D1 | Password hashing | Stored passwords are argon2 or bcrypt hashes (judge reads the seeded database) | 1 |\n| D2 | CSRF | Every state-changing form rejects a POST without a valid token (judge replays one POST per form without it; 2 = all rejected, 1 = ≥75%) | 2 |\n| D3 | Access-control tests | Tests exist that assert an editor gets 403 (or redirect) on every admin-only route and an anonymous visitor is redirected to login, and they pass (2 = all admin routes covered, 1 = some) | 2 |\n| D4 | Sanitized Markdown | Judge saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the admin preview and the export (2 = neither executes, 1 = one does) | 2 |\n| D5 | No secrets committed | No `.env`, `*.db`, keys, or tokens anywhere in history; `.env.example` present | 1 |\n\nA committed secret also triggers an immediate instructor notification, whatever the score.\n\n---\n\n#### E. Test & code quality — 8 pts\n\n**Definition:** the code the workflow produced is tested, organized, and runnable.\n**Does not cover:** whether the tests came from `/tdd` in the right order (B) or cover security specifically (D).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| E1 | Suite passes on clean clone | `uv run pytest` in the judge's container (3 = 100% pass, 2 = ≥95%, 1 = ≥80%) | 3 |\n| E2 | Tests trace to acceptance criteria | Judge samples 3 tickets; each acceptance criterion has ≥1 test that names or clearly exercises it (2 = all, 1 = ≥half) | 2 |\n| E3 | Organization | Code split by concern (models, routes, templates, services); no source file over 500 lines; no commented-out dead code blocks (2 = all three, 1 = two) | 2 |\n| E4 | Reproducible demo | `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean from `.env.example` values with no manual steps | 1 |\n\n---\n\n#### F. Public site & admin UX — 7 pts\n\n**Definition:** the public site and admin console load, link correctly, and are usable on a phone.\n**Does not cover:** feature correctness (C), or authenticity of design choices (A).\n\n| # | Item | Measure / how checked | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| F1 | Live over HTTPS | Pages URL loads over HTTPS | 1 |\n| F2 | Links and paths | Zero broken internal links and zero root-absolute paths on the published site (2 = zero, 1 = ≤3) | 2 |\n| F3 | Phone width | No horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page and 3 admin screens (2 = all, 1 = ≥half) | 2 |\n| F4 | Admin usability | Clear labels, a success or error message after each save, persistent admin navigation (2 = all three, 1 = two) | 2 |\n\n---\n\n#### G. {"parentUuid":"08188ed5-8051-4ebc-93ef-3c71319b0d4f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0d52ee7d-08c6-4e49-bfa6-27510dbf793e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: T01 (#2): login, sessions, CSRF, leader-only route declaration, users list. Seam: HTTP interface via FastAPI TestClient against a fresh temp SQLite DB per test."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"03984392-b438-495c-9175-d0519716d25b","timestamp":"2026-10-10T19:06:18.029Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_012ipuUNs6RTRhoDg18g13Mu","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c3c74ce2-0883-49ee-be0b-48ee718b4c6e","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Passwords come from\n# the environment there; in tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"lider@albiazul.example\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\",\n              \"nickname\": \"El Capi\", \"role\": \"admin\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"ana@albiazul.example\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\",\n               \"nickname\": \"Rayada de Corazón\", role=row[\"role\"], active=bool(row[\"active\"]))\n\n\ndef create_user(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, email: str, password: str, role: str,\n                nickname: str | None = None, active: bool = assert user is not None\n    return user\n\n\ndef get_user(conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: int | None) -> User | None:\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (#2): the demo seed and `.env.example`.\n\nEach test name says which acceptance criterion of #2 it covers.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef env_example() -> dict[str, str]:\n    pairs = (line.split(\"=\", 1) for line in (ROOT / \".env.example\").read_text().splitlines()\n             if line.strip() and not line.startswith(\"#\"))\n    return {key.strip(): value.strip() for key, value in pairs}\n\n\ndef run_seed(database: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(\"CMS_\")}\n    env |= env_example() | {\"CMS_DATABASE\": str(database)}\n    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, \"scripts/seed_demo.py\"], cwd=ROOT, env=env,\n                          capture_output=True, text=True)\n\n\ndef test_env_example_sets_site_title_and_student_placeholder():\n    values = env_example()\n\n    assert values[\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\"] == \"Club de Aficionados Albiazul\"\n    assert values[\"CMS_STUDENT\"] == \"first-last\"\n\n\ndef test_seed_runs_clean_from_env_example_and_its_users_log_in_by_nickname(\n        tmp_path, login, demo_users):\n    database = tmp_path / \"seeded.db\"\n    passwords = {\"admin\": env_example()[\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"],\n                 \"editor\": env_example()[\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"],\n                 \"editor2\": env_example()[\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"]}\n\n    for _ in range(2):  # the seed wipes and rebuilds, so a second run is clean too\n        result = run_seed(database)\n        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr\n    assert not any(p in result.stdout + result.stderr for p in passwords.values())\n\n    for role, user in demo_users.items():\n        c = TestClient(create_app(database))\n        assert login(c, user[\"email\"], passwords[role]).status_code == 303, role\n        assert user[\"nickname\"] in c.get(\"/admin\").text\n\n\ndef test_seed_creates_the_leader_and_two_members_matching_the_test_helper(\n        tmp_path, login, demo_users):\n    database = tmp_path / \"seeded.db\"\n    assert run_seed(database).returncode == 0\n    leader = TestClient(create_app(database))\n    login(leader, \"lider@albiazul.example\", env_example()[\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"])\n\n    page = leader.get(\"/admin/users\").text\n\n    assert page.count(\"@albiazul.example\") == 3\n    assert page.count(\"<td>Líder</td>\") == 1 and page.count(\"<td>Miembro</td>\") == 2\n    for user in demo_users.values():\n        assert f\"<td>{user['email']}</td>\" in page\n        assert f\"<td>{user['nickname']}</td>\" in page\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":352,"cache_read_input_tokens":149885,"output_tokens":3569,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2257},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":352,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3569,"cache_read_input_tokens":149885,"cache_creation_input_tokens":352,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":352},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_016118X2ikASnHAyenwBrKBN":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t01_seed.py","content":"\"\"\"T01 On a fresh clone\n# with no .env, the app and the seed read this file instead.\nCMS_SECRET_KEY=change-me-to-a-long-random-string\nCMS_SITE_TITLE=Club de Aficionados Albiazul\nCMS_DATABASE=cms.db\n# Demo accounts created by scripts/seed_demo.py (both members share the editor password)\nCMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin\nCMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor\n# Set after you deploy, e.g. https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nCMS_BASE_PATH=\n# Your name for the transcript hook, lowercase, e.g. ana-garcia\nCMS_STUDENT=first-last\nEOF\ncat > app/settings.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\n\nValues come from the real environment first, then from `.env`, then (on a fresh\nclone with no `.env`) from `.env.example`, so the seed and `cms serve` run with no\nmanual steps.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\n\ndef _load_env_file() -> None:\n    path = ROOT / \".env\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        path = ROOT / \".env.example\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        return\n    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n        line = line.strip()\n        if line and not line.startswith(\"#\") and \"=\" in line:\n            key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n            os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip())\n\n\n_load_env_file()\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\n# A relative CMS_DATABASE is relative to the project folder, not the shell's.\nDATABASE_PATH = ROOT / os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", \"cms.db\")\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"Club de Aficionados Albiazul\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\nEOF\ncat > scripts/seed_demo.py <<'EOF'\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Rebuild the demo database from scratch, with fictional data only.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nWipes the database at CMS_DATABASE and creates the leader and two members.\nPasswords come from CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD (read from .env,\nor from .env.example on a fresh clone); they are never printed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom contextlib import closing\n\nfrom app import accounts, db, settings\n\n# (email, nickname, role, environment variable holding the password).\n# tests/conftest.py uses the same emails and nicknames.\nDEMO_ACCOUNTS = [\n    (\"lider@albiazul.example\", \"El Capi\", \"admin\", \"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\"),\n    (\"ana@albiazul.example\", \"Rayada de Corazón\", \"editor\", \"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"),\n    (\"beto@albiazul.example\", \"Furia del Cerro\", \"editor\", \"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\"),\n]\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    missing = sorted({var for *_, var in DEMO_ACCOUNTS if not os.environ.get(var)})\n    if missing:\n        print(f\"Set {', '.join(missing)} in .env (copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    path = settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    db.init(path)\n    with closing(db.connect(path)) as conn:\n        for email, nickname, role, var in DEMO_ACCOUNTS:\n            accounts.create_user(conn, email=email, password=os.environ[var],\n                                 role=role, nickname=nickname)\n\n    print(f\"Rebuilt {path} with these demo accounts:\")\n    for email, nickname, role, var in DEMO_ACCOUNTS:\n        print(f\"  {email:<26} {role:<7} {nickname}  (password: ${var})\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\nEOF\nuv run pytest -q tests/test_t01_seed.py 2>&1 | grep -E 'passed|failed|^E' | head -6","description":"Write {"parentUuid":"c2117bc4-dc03-4530-8853-b2f62c470caf","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"938fb082-605f-42fb-854a-b6b9ea629bc0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the uncommitted working-tree changes since HEAD (86f613c) for ticket T01, GitHub issue #2 (spec: issue #1). Use `git diff HEAD` (new files are marked intent-to-add). Exclude notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/ — not part of this ticket."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"ffcef468-5f58-4990-ad47-bb60fd670a2d","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:03:37.363Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01Lb51DQ1VCttJZxvWVV1hRg","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c3c74ce2-0883-49ee-be0b-48ee718b4c6e","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Code is split by concern: `accounts`/`db`, `routes/`, `policy`, `web`, templates.\n- Nothing conflicts with ADR-001, 002 or 003.\n\n**Judgement calls against documented standards**\n1. **`app/settings.py` `_load_env_file()`** falls back to the committed `.env.example`. Without a `.env`, `CMS_SECRET_KEY` silently becomes the public `change-me-to-a-long-random-string`. That sits badly with `CLAUDE.md` (\"Read secrets from the environment\") and spec §210 (\"`.env`, never committed\"). It isn't a regression: the old hard-coded default was just as public. It was likely done for rubric E4.\n2. **Two words for one concept.** `scripts/seed_demo.py` has `DEMO_ACCOUNTS` and `tests/conftest.py` has `DEMO_USERS` for the same three people. `CLAUDE.md` says \"update the glossary rather than using both\". The spec itself uses both words (Accounts module, User entity), so the cheapest fix is aligning these two constant names.\n\n**Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n- **Duplicated Code:**\n  - The KEY=VALUE parsing in `settings._load_env_file` is repeated in `tests/test_t01_seed.py::env_example()`.\n  - The same inactive-user block (`create_user(conn, email=\"baja@albiazul.example\", ... active=False)`) appears in both `test_t01_access.py` and `test_t01_login.py`. A fixture would fix it.\n  - `test_t01_login.py` checks `status_code == 303 and location.endswith(\"/login\")` inline three times, while `test_t01_access.py` already has `redirects_to_login()`.\n  - The demo roster is copied between the seed and conftest. The code comments admit it, and `test_seed_creates_..._matching_the_test_helper` guards it, so it is tolerable.\n- **Primitive Obsession:** the role is a bare `\"admin\"` string in `User.is_leader`, the SQL `ORDER BY role = 'admin'`, the schema CHECK, the seed tuples and conftest. It's small for now, but it will spread as later tickets add role checks.\n- **Mysterious Name (minor):**\n  - `accounts._user(row)` would read better as `_user_from_row`.\n  - `app/routes/admin.py` only holds the dashboard, and every route in the console is an admin route.\n\n**For the Spec reviewer: a gap, not a style issue.** `web.signed_in_user` reloads the user through `accounts.get_user`, whose query (`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?`) never checks `active`. So a user deactivated mid-session keeps working. Spec §33 and §156 say deactivation \"takes effect immediately\" on the next request. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no blocking gaps. All 44 tests pass, and every acceptance criterion in #2 is met except for one traceability gap (a). I also ran the seed in a scratch copy of the repo with no `.env` and the `CMS_*` variables unset. It exited 0 and built the three accounts. I checked an upper-case email at login and probed behaviour directly.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n- **One criterion has no test.** The criterion *\"Each test runs against its own fresh temporary database\"* exists only as the `database_path` fixture and the docstring in `conftest.py`. No test name covers it or checks that `cms.db` is never touched, but the spec says *\"each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one test whose name says which criterion it covers.\"* A small test asserting that data written in one test is absent in the next would fix it.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n\n- **None of T02–T08 was built.** No posts, pages, nickname screen or user-management operations appear in the diff.\n- **The `.env.example` fallback in `app/settings.py` is acceptable.** Loading `.env` is needed in any case, because nothing else loads it and the rubric's own run does `cp .env.example .env`. The fallback goes further than that and means the app runs on the committed placeholder secret key. The spec says secrets come *\"from the environment (`.env`, never committed)\"*, but E4's *\"no manual steps\"* justifies it, and the old default key was hard-coded too.\n- **The `test_t00` rewrite is acceptable.** It is forced by *\"An anonymous request to any admin route redirects to `/login`.\"*\n\n**(c) Implemented, but questionable**\n\n1. **Signed-in user handling is not in the Accounts module.** The spec gives Accounts *\"session handling, loading the current user on every request and rejecting deactivated users … Interface: … current_user(request)\"*. Here that work sits in `app/web.py::signed_in_user`, mixed in with the leader-only check. When T07 adds the deactivation check it will land in the web layer, not in Accounts.\n2. **Leaving deactivated sessions to T07 is acceptable.** T07 explicitly owns *\"an open session of a deactivated user is rejected on its next request.\"* I confirmed the gap is real: after setting `active=0`, an existing session still gets 200 on `/admin`. The fix is one condition (`or not user.active`) in a user lookup that already runs on every request.\n3. **A CSRF failure shows raw JSON.** The 403 body is `{\"detail\":\"Formulario caducado o no válido…\"}` rather than a page. The ticket only requires 403, but the spec says *\"Everything people see is in Spanish\"* and the leader is *\"not technical.\"* An expired form shows him raw JSON.\n4. **The CSRF check runs before the login check.** For a future anonymous admin POST with no token, *\"a POST without a valid token gets 403\"* wins over the redirect to `/login`. That is a defensible order and no admin POST routes exist yet. It is worth one line in the T07 notes.\n5. **`/login` has no admin menu, which is acceptable.** The contract lists `/login` under \"Admin routes\", and the criterion says *\"Every admin page shows the persistent Spanish admin menu.\"* A menu with *Salir* makes no sense for a signed-out visitor. The test only checks `/admin*` paths.\n\nConfirmed correct:\n- The session cookie is `httponly` and `samesite=lax`.\n- Email login ignores case.\n- The access test asserts that every name in `LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES` is a real route, so a typo cannot slip through.\n- The seed prints no passwords.\n- The CSRF test sends a POST to every route without a token.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>87961</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>10</tool_uses><duration_ms>146835</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

When T07 adds the deactivation check it will land in the web layer, not in Accounts.\n2. **Leaving deactivated sessions to T07 is acceptable.** T07 explicitly owns *\"an open session of a deactivated user is rejected on its next request.\"* I confirmed the gap is real: after setting `active=0`, an existing session still gets 200 on `/admin`. The fix is one condition (`or not user.active`) in a user lookup that already runs on every request.\n3. **A CSRF failure shows raw JSON.** The 403 body is `{\"detail\":\"Formulario caducado o no válido…\"}` rather than a page. The ticket only requires 403, but the spec says *\"Everything people see is in Spanish\"* and the leader is *\"not technical.\"* An expired form shows him raw JSON.\n4. **The CSRF check runs before the login check.** For a future anonymous admin POST with no token, *\"a POST without a valid token gets 403\"* wins over the redirect to `/login`. That is a defensible order and no admin POST routes exist yet. It is worth one line in the T07 notes.\n5. **`/login` has no admin menu, which is acceptable.** The contract lists `/login` under \"Admin routes\", and the criterion says *\"Every admin page shows the persistent Spanish admin menu.\"* A menu with *Salir* makes no sense for a signed-out visitor. The test only checks `/admin*` paths.\n\nConfirmed correct:\n- The session cookie is `httponly` and `samesite=lax`.\n- Email login ignores case.\n- The access test asserts that every name in `LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES` is a real route, so a typo cannot slip through.\n- The seed prints no passwords.\n- The CSRF test sends a POST to every route without a token.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>87961</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>10</tool_uses><duration_ms>146835</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"073592cb-7ef5-4a34-8193-937fa25bc21a","timestamp":"2026-10-10T20:06:30.803Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mv2tofsm-d9edcf93"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":4,"turnIndex":6},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c3c74ce2-0883-49ee-be0b-48ee718b4c6e","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Checked: relative paths (templates use `url_for` and contain no `href=\"/`), CSRF on every form, argon2 hashing with no password printed, nothing secret tracked, no new dependency, no file over 500 lines, no commented-out code, and no conflict with ADR-001, ADR-002 or ADR-003.\n\n| # | Finding | Kind | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| S1 | `settings._load_env_file()` falls back to the committed `.env.example`, so without a `.env` the secret key is the public placeholder | judgement call (CLAUDE.md: \"Read secrets from the environment\") | **Kept.** This is no regression: the old hard-coded default key was public too. The admin console is local only (ADR-001), and rubric E4 needs the seed to run with \"no manual steps\". A real `.env` or real environment variables always win. |\n| S2 | `DEMO_ACCOUNTS` in the seed vs `DEMO_USERS` in `conftest.py` for the same people | judgement call (CLAUDE.md: one word per concept) | **Fixed.** Renamed the seed's constant to `DEMO_USERS`. |\n| S3 | Duplicated test code: the inactive-user setup in two files, and the inline \"redirected to /login\" check repeated | smell: Duplicated Code | **Fixed.** Added `inactive_user` and `redirects_to_login` fixtures in `conftest.py`. |\n| S4 | The test's `env_example()` parser repeats the settings loader | smell: Duplicated Code | **Kept on purpose.** The test reads `.env.example` independently so its expected values don't come from the code under test. |\n| S5 | The demo roster is copied between the seed and the test helper | smell: Duplicated Code | **Kept.** `test_seed_creates_the_leader_and_two_members_matching_the_test_helper` guards that the two copies match. |\n| S6 | The role is a bare `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` string | smell: Primitive Obsession | **Deferred to T07** (#8), which adds role changes and is where role checks will spread. |\n| S7 | `accounts._user(row)`, and `routes/admin.py` holding only the dashboard | smell: Mysterious Name | **Fixed.** Renamed them to `_user_from_row` and `routes/dashboard.py`. |\n\n### Spec\n\nEvery acceptance criterion of #2 is met. Nothing from T02–T08 was built.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | \"Each test runs against its own fresh temporary database\" had no test whose name covers it (E2) | **Fixed.** Added `test_each_test_runs_against_its_own_fresh_temporary_database`, run twice; a shared database would make the second run fail. |\n| P2 | An open session of a deactivated user still worked, and current-user loading sat in the web layer instead of Accounts (\"loading the current user on every request and rejecting deactivated users\"). The Standards reviewer flagged this too. | **Fixed, test first.** Added `accounts.active_user()`, which the session gate now uses, and `test_open_session_of_a_deactivated_user_stops_working_on_next_request`. T07 still owns the deactivate button. |\n| P3 | A CSRF failure returned raw JSON (`{\"detail\": …}`) to a non-technical leader (\"Everything people see is in Spanish\") | **Fixed, test first.** A Spanish *Formulario caducado* page with status 403. |\n| P4 | The CSRF check runs before the login check, so an anonymous admin POST with no token gets 403 rather than a redirect | **Kept.** \"A POST without a valid token gets 403\" takes precedence, and anonymous POSTs that carry a valid token are still redirected (tested). |\n| P5 | `/login` shows no admin menu | **Kept.** A menu with *Salir* means nothing to someone signed out, and the menu test covers every `/admin*` page. |\n| P6 | `test_t00.py::test_admin_console_answers` changed | **Accepted by both reviewers.** T01 requires anonymous admin requests to redirect to `/login`. The test now checks that the leader's dashboard answers. |\n\n**Summary:** 7 Standards findings (the worst is S1, the placeholder secret key on a fresh clone; kept, with reasons) and 6 Spec findings (the worst is P2, sessions of deactivated users surviving; fixed).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1903,"cache_read_input_tokens":181686,"output_tokens":2042,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":67},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1903,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2042,"cache_read_input_tokens":181686,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1903,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1903},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01Cgx2CNBjcFt4p7TXQ3BpfH":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/c3c74ce2-0883-49ee-be0b-48ee718b4c6e/scratchpad/t01-review.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings for T01, and how each was resolved\n\nTwo-axis review (`mattpocock-skills:code-review`) of the working tree against `86f613c`. {"parentUuid":"6364db80-3946-4a85-b342-63b7a3ad7890","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ca4b0e31-b8d5-498a-a211-ad578e66915f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0176Kb442P5YvQoCVGd9hKey","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Token budget plan\n2\t\n3\tWritten 2026-10-10, before the first `/implement`. Plan in percent of my own\n4\tmeters (5-hour window and weekly cap), not tokens. Re-forecast with\n5\t`uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining N` after T01 and after T03.\n6\t\n7\t## Model plan\n8\t\n9\t| Stage | Model | Effort | Estimate (% of a 5-hour window) |\n10\t|---|---|---|---|\n11\t| `/research`, quick lookups | Haiku 4.5 | low | ~2% each |\n12\t| `/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets` | Opus 5.5 | xhigh | **actual: 16% for the grill (28 turns), ~2% for spec + tickets** |\n13\t| `/implement` + `/tdd` (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | medium | ~20% per ticket (T03 and T07 likely ~30%) |\n14\t| `/code-review` (per ticket) | Sonnet 5.5 | high | ~5% per ticket |\n15\t| Exercises A and B (`/tdd`) | Opus 5.5 | xhigh | ~2% total |\n16\t\n17\tPlanning ran on Opus 5.5 at xhigh because it was already my default. That is the\n18\texpensive end; everything from T01 on switches to Sonnet 5.5 (`/model`, then\n19\t`/effort medium`).\n20\t\n21\t## Forecast\n22\t\n23\t- **Tickets:** 8 core tickets × ~25% (implement + review) ≈ 200% of a window,\n24\t  so **about 2–3 five-hour windows**, assuming I `/clear` between tickets.\n25\t- **Weekly cap:** the grill spent 2% of the weekly cap for 16% of a window\n26\t  (about 1 : 8 on Opus). Sonnet should be cheaper per window, so I expect\n27\t  roughly 3% weekly per ticket, **about 25–30% of one week** for all 8. Weekly\n28\t  was at 4% when this plan was written.\n29\t- **Verdict:** fits, with room for one `stretch` ticket only if the T03\n30\t  re-forecast says FITS.\n31\t\n32\t## If I am wrong, cut in this order\n33\t\n34\t1. Lower effort on `/implement` (medium → low) for the mechanical tickets\n35\t   (T04, T06).\n36\t2. Drop the `stretch` ticket.\n37\t3.
